newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly lower on low volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly lower on low volumes.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly lower Friday, with gold and silver down for the third day in a row, leaving the complex finishing the week on a bearish note, analysts said.

"There wasn't much activity today, but the the market ended the week looking soft, despite some shortcovering of locals near the close," North American Equity Services floor trader John Geraghty said.
COMEX December gold ended down 50 cents at $382.10 an ounce, slipping to a two week intraday low at $381.60.
However, COMEX gold stocks fell 965 ounces to 1,053,329 ounces Thursday, and are at their lowest levels since November 1977.
In New York bullion trade, gold ended quoted $380.10/380.50, against the London Friday afternoon fix at $380.00, and the New York close Thursday at $380.35/380.85.
But the key $380 support level, which has held since April 1995, remained intact again Friday, traders noted.
COMEX December silver ended down 0.5 cent at $4.897 an ounce, though Thursday's intraday low at $4.880 was not breached.
COMEX silver stocks were unchanged Thursday at 130,794,680, after seeing a ten year low earlier this week, but traders said inventories in other countries were ample.
The spot gold/silver ratio ended at 77.7, little changed from Thursday's close, after a the ratio fell to 75.4 in the past week, when silver was recovering.

Fabricators have seen some value around current price levels for precious metals in the past ten days, helping prices to recovery, but with investor demand weak, funds have been able to sell the precious metals back down on light volume in the past two days, analysts said.
NYMEX January platinum closed unchanged at $388.30 an ounce, while NYMEX December palladium ended up 75 cents at $117.25 an ounce.
But in the bullion market, physical palladium fixed at a three and a half year low at $115.25 an ounce in London Friday.

"There has been some speculation that political events in Russia, regarding the now former national security advisor Mr Lebed, had a negative impact on palladium this week, but it is more probable that renewed short selling was the main reason palladium slid further," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
--Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
